title: mood-policy.json
description: The mood-mode policy store (LEO-236). One definitional store, keyed by the six mood ids the focus store enumerates, recording what each mood allows, changes, or suppresses across notifications, launches, background work, and the reachability of named workspace scenes. `focus.json` stays the *active* state ({ mode, until }); this file is what a mode *means*, so both runtimes — Quickshell's Focus/Notify, Hyprland Lua's event manager, and the launcher scripts on $PATH — read one policy instead of each re-inventing one. The defaults deliberately reproduce today's behavior (the firm focus gate, per-mood notification policies from Focus.qml) so adopting the store changes nothing until LEO-237 exposes it and LEO-238 enforces it.

moods.description: Per-mood policy. Keys are the mood ids the focus store enumerates (neutral, deep, chores, reflect, game, media). Visual knobs live here too: a mood is a visual operating state — a palette accent role and a surface alpha — not just a notification switch, and Focus.qml already) owns that table. Palette/policy divergence between this file and Focus.qml is a deployment bug; the lockstep test pins it, and LEO-237 makes this store the source Focus.qml mirrors.

accent_role.description: A semantic role on the active palette (Theme.c.<role>), never a literal colour — the palette stays the source of truth and a mood only picks which of its roles takes the spotlight.

surface_alpha.description: The one dial this mood turns on the shared card material; paper, not glass.

density.description: How much the shell lets crowd a surface.

motion_energy.description: How animated the shell feels in this mood.

bar_autohide.description: Whether the bar drops to the bare indicators (workspace, submap, clock) in this mood.

notificationPolicy.description: The toast policy: what is allowed to appear on screen. Suppression is toast-only — history keeps recording, which is what `queue` and `digest_on_exit` exist for.

queue.description: Buffer toasts behind the current one while suppressed, for digest-on-exit.

digest_on_exit.description: Emit one digest notification when the mood ends.

launchPolicy.description: Refuse-to-start policy for media/game launchers, read at dispatch time by ,focus-guard.sh and the launchers. Never touches an already-running session. `soft` notifies and lets through; `firm` refuses with a reason and honours the override key; `hard` refuses until the mood ends. Open decision #3 resolves here per mood; the defaults are the current firm behavior.

block.description: Launch categories refused while this mood is active. A mood never lists itself — entering `game` is how you start gaming, so it cannot also refuse the game launch that got you there.

override.description: Firm moods may name an explicit override key that lets a blocked launch through. false for soft (nothing is blocked) and hard (refusal is unconditional).

backgroundPolicy.description: Background-work rules for the user systemd timers and services the desk runs (theme-auto, obsidian index/sync, state-backup, chezmoi externals, audio-notify). `allow` lists what runs; `defer` what waits for a friendlier window; `prevent` what must not start. The defaults allow everything — adopting the store must not change behavior until the shell (LEO-237) or runtime policy (LEO-238) restricts something.

scenePolicy.description: Reachability of each named workspace scene (scenes.json) while this mood is active. Absent = reachable, so the resting mood is an empty object and a focus mood only names what it takes away. `blocked` makes the scene unreachable (its window rules still hold for an already-open session — enforcement is at dispatch, never teardown); `limited` keeps it reachable with the mood's restrictions applied. Binding context reads the same map, so which-key can dim a scene's binds while it is blocked.
